newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares hit record highs in late dealings.
newsitem.headline: German shares hit record highs in late dealings.

text.p: German share prices rose on Thursday to drive the IBIS DAX index to a new all-time high of 3,944.34 in late trade, with dealers' sights firmly set on breaking the 4,000 level in the coming weeks.

The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings in the top 30 shares, ended at 3,939.73, up 1.87 percent or 72.20 points from Wednesday's close, after vaulting 3,900 in reponse to a key U.S. employment report which pointed to modest growth in wages and new jobs.

The 30-share DAX index had ended the floor-trading session up 32.63 points at 3,887.39 points before the 1230 GMT June jobs report which showed payrolls rose by 217,000 while the unemployment rate ticked up to 5.0 percent from 4.8 percent.
The news helped boost U.S. bond and share prices, with the Dow Jones index up 90.93 points at 7,886.31 at 1550 GMT.
The higher dollar was underpinning export-sensitive shares, particularly in the chemical and automotive sectors, as traders said the DAX could break 4,000 points in the next few weeks.
Chemicals giant Hoechst AG ended up 1.60 marks or two percent at 80.30 marks.

The top gainer was luxury carmaker Porsche AG, which ended electronic dealings up 6.96 percent or 175 marks at 2,690 marks. Brokerage house Lehman said this week it set a price target for Porsche at 3,600 marks.
Airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG rose 6.17 percent or two marks to 34.40 marks while carmaker Volkswage AG was up 4.99 percent at 1,402 marks.
